# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can physically cut wires 1–3, but I have no tactile distinction or instruction yet. Mute has the manual and Deaf has the visible bomb markings, so Mute needs to use a gesture protocol with Deaf, who can then speak the resulting instruction to me.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I can cut wire positions 1, 2, or 3, but have no other tactile information. Please use the manual's gesture instructions to communicate with Deaf, and have Deaf relay the exact cut instruction to me by voice.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb view: DISPLAY 0. LIGHT yellow. WIRES ordered 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute has the manual; follow their spoken instruction.

Deaf has identified the visible configuration: display 0, yellow light, and wires in order blue, red, green. Mute can hear my voice and has the manual, so I should relay these observations exactly and await the manual-derived cut instruction.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display 0; light yellow; wires: position 1 blue, position 2 red, position 3 green. Please tell Deaf by gesture which position I must cut, and have Deaf relay it to me by voice.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current bomb view: display 0; light blue; wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute just gestured exactly: up-pointing index finger, up-pointing index finger, up-pointing index finger.

Mute’s three repeated up-pointing gestures appear to be an encoded cut instruction, but Deaf now reports that the light has changed from yellow to blue. That may alter the manual’s rule, so I should not cut based on the earlier signal. I need Mute to recompute using the current state.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Do not rely on the prior instruction yet: Deaf now reports the light is blue, not yellow. Current visible state remains display 0; wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Please recalculate from the manual and gesture the current cut position to Deaf for verbal relay.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current bomb view: display 0; light white; wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute just gestured exactly one raised open hand (?).

The light has changed again, now to white. The open-hand gesture is not an unambiguous wire-position instruction to me, especially since there are only three possible cuts. I will not cut until Mute provides a clear position encoding based on the current state.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf now reports: display 0, light white, wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. I cannot safely interpret one open-hand gesture as a wire position. For the current state, please signal the cut position unambiguously to Deaf: one raised index for wire 1, two fingers for wire 2, three fingers for wire 3; or signal no cut/wait with an open hand.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current bomb view: display 0; light red; wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute just signalled two raised open hands, identical to the single raised open-hand signal from last turn but repeated twice.

The bomb’s light is now red. Mute’s repeated open-hand signal still does not identify one of the three wire positions under the encoding I proposed, and the changing light may be relevant to the manual. I will wait and ask Mute to use a stable, explicit cut-position signal for the current state rather than guessing.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Current state from Deaf: display 0; light red; wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Your two repeated open-hand gestures are not a safe wire number for me. Please, when the manual says to cut, gesture exactly: ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, or three raised fingers for wire 3. Use 🖐 only to mean wait/no cut. Deaf will say the gesture aloud to me.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current bomb view: display 0; light purple; wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute just signalled one spread open hand (?), distinct from the earlier raised open-hand gesture (?).

Mute’s latest gesture is still outside the explicit cut-position code I proposed, so it cannot safely authorize a cut. The light continues to cycle, and Mute can only calculate from the most recently relayed observation. I will send a strict, symbol-level protocol for the next manual answer and wait for Deaf’s verbal relay.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I need one unambiguous final instruction, based on the latest state you received. Use exactly one gesture symbol only: ☝ means cut position 1; ✌ means cut position 2; 🖖 means cut position 3; 🖐 means wait/no cut. Do not use any other gesture. Deaf should relay the exact symbol and I will act only on ☝, ✌, or 🖖.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current bomb view: display 0; light yellow; wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute again signalled one spread open hand (?), the same gesture as last turn.

The repeated spread-hand gesture is not one of the cut codes I proposed, so it is not an agreed authorization to cut. It may be part of Mute’s own manual-based signalling, but neither Deaf nor I has been given its meaning. I will ask Mute to acknowledge the agreed code before issuing a cut instruction; until then, cutting would be a guess.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I still cannot decode the spread-hand sign. Please first gesture 🖐 once to acknowledge this agreed code: ☝ = cut wire 1; ✌ = cut wire 2; 🖖 = cut wire 3; 🖐 = wait. On a later turn, send exactly the applicable one-symbol instruction based on the current bomb state. Do not send a cut symbol unless it is final.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current bomb view: display 0; light blue; wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute just signalled one Vulcan-salute hand gesture (?), distinct from prior signals.

Mute has now used the agreed one-symbol code: the Vulcan salute, 🖖, means cut wire position 3. I will cut wire 3.

```text
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
